newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA COUNTS DOWN TO LAUNCH OF BINGO INDUSTRY.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA COUNTS DOWN TO LAUNCH OF BINGO INDUSTRY.

text.p: The shout of "bingo" will soon be heard in South Africa and firms are unveiling multi-million rand plans for gaming centres after legislation last year legalised casino gambling for the first time.
Bingo Vision, a gaming consultancy firm with British and South African shareholders, was launched on Thursday with pledges of hefty investments, job creation and a sea of winners.
Managing director Steve McCain estimated that South Africa will have 300 bingo centres in operation by 2000, each generating 10 million rand per annum and creating a total of 45,000 jobs.
"The first bingo club could be up and running before the end of the year," McCain said.

Provincial authorities, which have been given the reins to run gaming, have almost completed the necessary legislation to control the industry. Mpumulanga province said it would be calling for bingo licence applications by next month.

Bingo Vision said on Thursday it would invest an initial 10 million rand in setting up bingo centres. A further five million rand would be allocated for the next few months of operation and ongoing investment of between three and seven million rand would be put up for each new venue.

The South African investment by the group, which says it is responsible for new bingo industries in Russia, Romania, Argentina and Brazil, is backed by British firm Edward Thompson and Spanish company Vaprel.
The low-stakes game of bingo, which originated in China, has become particularly popular in the United Kingdom where it contributes some one billion rand annually to government coffers, McCain said.

"Bingo is a leisure game which is played from South America to Australia and from Russia to Romania because it is affordable and provides a social setting for people to meet in an enjoyable leisure activity," he said.
